Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 1) Primary Health Care was declared at:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Primary Health Care was declared at Alma-Ata. It emphasized essential health care for all. It promoted equity, community participation and intersectoral action.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 2) Alma-Ata Declaration was held in:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Alma-Ata Declaration was held in 1978. It is a landmark event in public health. It established Primary Health Care as the key strategy for “Health for All.”

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 3) Primary Health Care mainly means:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.option1: Essential health care made universally accessible
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: PHC means essential health care. It should be universally accessible and acceptable. It is based on practical, scientifically sound and socially acceptable methods.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 4) One key principle of Primary Health Care is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Community participation is a core principle of PHC. People should be involved in planning and using health services. This improves acceptance and sustainability.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 5) Intersectoral coordination in Primary Health Care means coordination between:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.option4: Health sector and other development sectors
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Health depends on many sectors such as education, agriculture, housing, sanitation and transport. Intersectoral coordination means these sectors work together. Medical services alone cannot solve all health problems.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 6) Appropriate technology in Primary Health Care means technology that is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Appropriate technology should fit local needs and resources. It should be scientifically sound but affordable. ORS is a classic example.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 7) Equitable distribution in Primary Health Care means:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.option1: Health care according to need, especially underserved groups
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.option2: Health services mainly for rich people
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Equitable distribution means health care should reach those who need it most. It reduces health inequality. Rural, poor and vulnerable groups should not be excluded.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 8) The first level of contact between individual and health system is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Primary care is the first contact level. It provides basic preventive, promotive and curative care. It also refers patients when higher care is needed.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 9) Referral system in health care mainly means:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.option1: Sending every patient to tertiary hospital directly
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.option4: Movement of patient from one level of care to another when needed
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: Referral links primary, secondary and tertiary care. Patients are managed at the appropriate level. A good referral system improves continuity and efficiency of care.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 10) Millennium Development Goals were launched in:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: MDGs were launched in 2000. They continued up to 2015. They mainly focused on developing countries.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 11) Sustainable Development Goals were launched in:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs were launched in 2015. They replaced MDGs after 2015. Their target year is 2030.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 12) MDGs ended in:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: MDGs ran from 2000 to 2015. After that, SDGs were adopted. MDGs had fewer goals and targets than SDGs.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 13) SDGs are targeted to be achieved by:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs aim to achieve targets by 2030. They cover health, poverty, education, environment and equity. They are broader than MDGs.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 14) Total number of MDGs was:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: MDGs had 8 goals. They focused mainly on poverty, health and education. SDGs later expanded the development agenda.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 15) Total number of SDGs is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs have 17 goals. They include both health and non-health development areas. They are universal for all countries.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 16) Total number of MDG targets was:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: MDGs had 18 targets. They had fewer targets than SDGs. The monitoring system was simpler.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 17) Total number of SDG targets is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs have 169 targets. They are more detailed than MDGs. They also require stronger monitoring systems.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 18) MDGs were mainly focused on:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: MDGs mainly focused on developing countries. They emphasized poverty, health and education. SDGs later became universal for all countries.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 19) SDGs are applicable to:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs are universal. They apply to both developed and developing countries. Their approach is broader and more inclusive.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 20) The main health-related SDG is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDG Goal 3 is mainly related to health. It focuses on ensuring healthy lives. It also promotes well-being for all ages.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 21) The slogan strongly associated with SDGs is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs emphasize inclusiveness. “Leave no one behind” reflects equity and universal coverage. It aims to reduce inequality in development.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 22) MDG approach was mainly:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: MDG approach was top-down and donor-driven. SDG approach is more participatory. This is an important difference between MDG and SDG.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 23) SDG approach is best described as:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs follow a participatory and inclusive approach. They focus on equity and broader development. Monitoring is also more robust.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 24) MDG monitoring was:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: MDG monitoring was simpler and less detailed. SDGs use more robust monitoring with data systems. This reflects the broader scope of SDGs.

Primary health care, SDG , MDG.question: 25) The SDG monitoring system is:
Primary health care, SDG , MDG.exp: SDGs have more detailed monitoring. They use broader indicators and data systems. This supports accountability across many sectors.
